clue.text: Escape by following cliff

indicators.note: following places the word for by after the word for cliff

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff or crag, especially in northern England
per means by, as in per post or as per instructions

explanation.surface: A fugitive gets away by keeping to the line of the cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' only fixes the order of the two pieces. Splitting after the fifth letter is tempting, since that also gives a word for a cliff, but it strands the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: to run away quickly, to make off.

clue.text: In music, Klemperer used to cut a swathe

indicators.note: In says the answer lies inside the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: The conductor Otto Klemperer made a big impression in the musical world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals letters running across the join of 'music' and 'Klemperer'. To cut a swathe is figuratively to make a splash, but here it is literal mowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved-bladed hand tool for reaping, so it literally mows a strip of grass or corn.

clue.text: Hospital worker with a pound — a lot of money, right?

parts.note: L is the old abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most of it, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone on a hospital's staff thinks a pound is a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' takes most of 'money', leaving MONE. In British hospitals this was the old title for a medical social worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical job title: the official in a British hospital who looked after patients' welfare and payments.

clue.text: In less debauched surroundings, Charles might be a customer

indicators.note: surroundings says the word for less debauched goes around the name

parts.note: purer means more chaste, so less debauched

explanation.surface: In more wholesome company, Charles might actually pay for things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In ... surroundings' frames the short form of the name with the comparative adjective; 'might be' is just the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a buyer is someone who pays a shop for goods.

clue.text: Formidable fortification finally accomplished

indicators.note: finally places the word for accomplished at the end, after the fortification

parts.note: a redoubt is a small defensive earthwork or stronghold
an accomplished performer is an able one

explanation.surface: An imposing stronghold has at last been completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' only fixes the order: ABLE comes last. 'accomplished' reads as a verb but works as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: inspiring respect or fear, as a daunting opponent does.

clue.text: Business backed by leading American organization with many branches

indicators.note: backed means the abbreviation for business is written backwards

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
the leading player is the top one
US is used adjectivally for American

explanation.surface: A firm with offices everywhere has the support of a major American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns CO into OC. The word is used figuratively for a far-reaching organisation whose branches are its tentacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a sprawling body with tentacles reaching everywhere, and the animal itself has eight arms.

clue.text: Poem due to be recited

indicators.note: to be recited means the word for due is spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: money that is due is owed

explanation.surface: A piece of verse is scheduled for a public reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a lyric verse form addressed to a person or thing.

clue.text: Coach takes up training of raw beginners

indicators.note: beginners points to the starting letters of the five preceding words

explanation.surface: A trainer starts teaching complete novices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginners' asks for the starting letters of 'takes up training of raw'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verb or noun: to give someone private teaching.

clue.text: Procession takes long, long time entering

indicators.note: entering says the word for a long time goes inside the word for long

parts.note: to long for something is to pant for it
an age is a long time, as in it took an age

explanation.surface: A parade spends ages getting into the arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' is the insertion signal. The first 'long' is a verb meaning yearn, not a length of time; only the second is about duration.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a colourful parade or spectacle, often in costume.

clue.text: A good man, the warden — you don't know him

parts.note: St, short for saint, is the crossword good man
a ranger is the warden of a park or forest

explanation.surface: The warden is a decent chap, though nobody here has met him.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a person who is unfamiliar to you.

clue.text: About a thousand attend game in city

indicators.note: attend says the first two pieces accompany the game, standing beside it

parts.note: ca is short for circa, meaning about
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Roughly a thousand spectators turn up for a match in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an English university town with city status.

clue.text: Wild cat — it's seen around Germany

indicators.note: seen around means the pronoun is turned round and read from the other end

parts.note: the word it, without its apostrophe s

explanation.surface: A big cat has been spotted roaming Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen around' looks like a container signal wrapping the country, but it only turns the pronoun round; the country's abbreviation simply follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large striped feline living wild in Asia.

clue.text: Start off without a meal

indicators.note: without says the letter that follows is taken out of the word for start off

parts.note: to launch a project is to start it off

explanation.surface: Someone sets out on a journey having had nothing to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A from LAUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the food eaten in the middle of the day.

clue.text: It's chancy when some, but not all, follow one abroad

indicators.note: follow places the word for some after the foreign word for one

parts.note: un is the French for one
certain people means some of them, not all

explanation.surface: It is risky when only part of a tour group trails after its leader overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follow' only fixes the order. 'abroad' asks for a foreign word, here French, and 'It's' and 'when' join definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: risky, with the outcome in doubt.

clue.text: Hip supporter of American football

parts.note: hip is the cry in hip hip hooray, so this is someone who leads the shouting for a US football team

explanation.surface: A fashionable fan of gridiron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hip' looks like trendy, or a joint needing support; it is the shout that starts 'hip, hip, hooray'.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: the person on the sidelines directing the crowd's chants at US sports.

clue.text: Tackle a difficulty boldly — you may get stung if you do

definitions.meaning: the idiom for dealing firmly and at once with an awkward problem

definitions.text: you may get stung if you do
definitions.meaning: taken literally, seizing this stinging weed in your hand could hurt

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom and its literal reading: the phrase means facing a problem head on, and literally describes seizing a stinging plant.

clue.text: Infatuated, displaying peculiar demeanour

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the letters of the next word are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone smitten is behaving strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' rearranges 'demeanour'; 'displaying' just links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: captivated, head over heels in love.

clue.text: Dyed-in-the-wool foundation

definitions.meaning: describes the most committed, unchanging members of a group
the broken brick and rubble laid as a base under roads and buildings

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the adjective for uncompromising devotees, and the noun for rubble forming the base of a road.

clue.text: The northern lights should appear here — or is Labour area in a mess?

indicators.note: in a mess says the letters of the four words before it are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A stargazer wonders whether a Labour-voting district has gone to ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mess' rearranges 'or is Labour area'. Labour is one of Britain's main political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: the Latin term for the glowing display in Arctic skies.

clue.text: Sign preceding a leaf in the storm?

indicators.note: preceding places the sign before the word for a leaf

parts.note: the Ram is the zodiac sign Aries
a leaf of a book is a page

explanation.surface: An omen comes just before a leaf is blown about in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preceding' only fixes the order. 'storm' is a verb here, to rage about, and the sign is one of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verb: to rush about violently and angrily.

clue.text: Careless smoker I found annoying

indicators.note: careless suggests sloppy handling, so the letters that follow are disarranged

explanation.surface: I came across a thoughtless smoker who got on my nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Careless' rearranges 'smoker' and 'I' together.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tiresome, getting on one's nerves.

clue.text: Take a carriage south for French city

parts.note: mien is a person's bearing, the way they carry themselves

explanation.surface: A traveller rides a coach southwards to a town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' is not a vehicle but a person's bearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the cathedral town on the Somme in northern France.

clue.text: Hold back a setting for ornament in metal

parts.note: to dam a river is to hold its water back
the scene of a story is its setting

explanation.surface: A jeweller keeps aside a mount meant for a metal decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ornament' is a verb in the definition: to inlay steel with wavy patterns of gold or silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to decorate steel or iron with inlaid wavy patterns, a craft named after Syria's capital.

clue.text: Neat guide

definitions.meaning: neat is an old word for cattle, of which a young castrated ox is one
to direct the course of a vehicle or a person

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a bullock is an example of the archaic cattle word, and the verb means to direct a course.

clue.text: It was used for caulking in former county town, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the town's name is spoken and another spelling is heard

parts.note: Oakham was the county town of Rutland, England's smallest county, abolished in 1974 and later restored

explanation.surface: Sailors' sealing material was once stored in an old county capital, by all accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes it a soundalike of OAKHAM, the chief town of Rutland, a tiny English county that lost its status in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: loose fibre from old rope, hammered into the seams of wooden ships to make them watertight.

clue.text: Make a speech elaborate, but miss the point

indicators.note: but miss says the word for elaborate loses the compass point

parts.note: ornate means elaborately decorated
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A speaker gives a long, fancy address without ever getting to the heart of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but miss' removes N from ORNATE. 'elaborate' looks like a verb but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to hold forth formally in public.

clue.text: US to order new emblem of royalty

indicators.note: new says the letters of the three words before it are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: America is going to commission a fresh royal badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges 'US to order'. It is the red-and-white heraldic flower of England's Tudor monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the heraldic flower badge adopted by Henry VII and still a symbol of England's crown.

clue.text: Pull, having hit with the wrong part of club, say

indicators.note: say means the golfing word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.words: hit with the wrong part of club
parts.note: in golf, to toe the ball is to strike it with the tip of the clubhead instead of the middle

explanation.surface: A golfer hooks a shot left after mishitting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes it a soundalike of TOE. A pull is also a golf shot that goes off line, which hides the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to drag something along behind.

clue.text: It might be raised, were boy to become silly

indicators.note: to become silly says the letters of the two words before it lose their sensible order

explanation.surface: Someone might object if the lad started acting the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become silly' rearranges 'were boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: the strip of hair above the eye that lifts in surprise or disapproval.

clue.text: It's a relief to change one's clothes

definitions.meaning: relief in the legal sense of a remedy or compensation for a wrong
read with a hyphen after the first two letters, it means to put clothes on again

explanation.definitionFit: Two readings: a remedy for a grievance, and whimsically putting on a fresh outfit.
